source_context_translations.translation: The Way that can be spoken is not the constant Way; the name that can be named is not the constant name.
Without names, Heaven and earth began; with names, they are the mother of the ten thousand things.
Therefore, constantly without desire, one observes its subtlety.
Constantly with desire, one observes its manifestations.
These two arise from the same source but have different names; together they are called mysterious.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To express something in words or discourse.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): This verbal use contrasts with the preceding noun sense of the Way.
Sentence Translations (English): The Way that can be spoken is not the constant Way.
The sage speaks of virtue without contention.
I state its cause to the ruler.
In antiquity, people were guided through virtue.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The underlying course or principle through which things arise and proceed, beyond complete verbal definition.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it is the ineffable cosmic Way, not merely a spoken doctrine or physical road.
contextual_sense.Register (English): Laozi philosophical and literary language, transmitted in the Wang Bi recension

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Expresses suitability or worthiness for a particular judgment or action.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): This evaluative use means that something merits approval or acceptance.
Sentence Translations (English): These words are worth hearing.
That man is fit for use.
This course is practicable.
The crime is not pardonable.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates that an action is possible or can successfully be performed.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): It marks possibility rather than permission in this passage.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To judge a claim or action to be erroneous or unacceptable.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): Unlike simple negation, this use conveys criticism or rejection.
Sentence Translations (English): The ruler rejects his statement.
Everyone condemns him.
He rejects antiquity and approves the present.
I dare not reject the former kings.
additional_senses.Translation (English): to deny; to reject as wrong

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Negates the following phrase or assertion.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): It is a direct classical negator, especially common before nominal or verbal predicates.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The enduring cosmic principle that does not change with particular descriptions or circumstances.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): 常 marks permanence and constancy, not ordinary frequency.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To assign or use a verbal designation for someone or something.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): This is the verbal use of the same graph in the following phrase.
Sentence Translations (English): He names it the Way.
He names his son Ming.
It cannot be named.
I designate his offense.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A designation assigned to an entity so that it can be identified or discussed.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): The passage contrasts names with what they attempt to designate.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A designation that remains universally and permanently adequate to what it identifies.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): It implies a name whose adequacy is not limited by changing conditions.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): States that a person or thing is absent or nonexistent in a given situation.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): This existential use focuses on absence rather than possession.
Sentence Translations (English): There are no worthy men in the state.
There is no one in the mountains.
There is no Way under Heaven.
There is no master in the chamber.
additional_senses.Translation (English): there is not; does not exist

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Expresses the absence or non-possession of something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it means absence of a name, not simple negation of an action.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The encompassing cosmic order and the terrestrial world considered together.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): The pair denotes the whole natural cosmos, not merely sky and soil.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A grammatical linker marking a possessive, attributive, or nominal relationship.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it links Heaven and earth to their beginning.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To commence an action, process, or state.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): The verbal use denotes initiating rather than the starting point itself.
Sentence Translations (English): Spring begins to arrive.
The king begins governing the state.
The people begin to understand ritual.
The rain begins to fall.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The initial point from which a process or sequence starts.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it is the cosmic beginning, prior to the emergence of named things.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To hold, own, or be endowed with something.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): This use emphasizes possession by a subject rather than bare existence.
Sentence Translations (English): The people possess fields.
The ruler possesses virtue.
The state has laws.
The household has a worthy son.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Marks the presence or existence of something, here the existence of names.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): It contrasts with 無 as presence or formed existence contrasts with absence.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): All differentiated beings and phenomena in the manifest cosmos.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): The phrase is an idiom for the totality of created or observable things.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To nurture, generate, or care for something in the manner of a mother.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): This verbal use is figurative and emphasizes generative care.
Sentence Translations (English): Heaven and earth mother the ten thousand things.
The queen mothers her people.
Virtue nurtures all under Heaven.
A loving mother cares for the orphan.
additional_senses.Translation (English): to serve as a mother; to mother

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A female parent, or metaphorically the generating source from which things arise.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here 母 is metaphorical: named existence generates and nourishes the ten thousand things.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Introduces a conclusion or consequence drawn from what precedes.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): It marks a reasoned transition, not a temporal ‘formerly.’

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates that a state or practice is maintained continuously or habitually.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it modifies 無欲 and contrasts with the passage’s 有欲 observation.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To wish for or seek something as an object of inclination.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): The verbal use presents desire as an active mental impulse.
Sentence Translations (English): People desire wealth and rank.
The ruler wants to govern the people.
I want to study the Way.
Everyone wants to obtain it.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A directed inclination toward obtaining or experiencing something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): In Laozi, desire often means acquisitive or discriminating want that affects perception.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Introduces the means or purpose by which the following action is performed.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it links freedom from desire with the purpose of observing subtlety.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To examine something by looking at it carefully.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): This concrete use focuses on visual examination rather than inward contemplation.
Sentence Translations (English): The ruler observes the people’s condition.
The envoy inspects the market.
The scholar examines his book.
The ruler views the water at the river.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To attend to and discern something through deliberate contemplation.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): It suggests contemplative perception, not merely casual looking.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A third-person possessive or attributive pronoun referring to the previously mentioned object.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): It refers back to the Way or the object under contemplation without naming it again.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Marked by an extraordinary quality that inspires admiration.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): This adjectival use praises an observable quality rather than naming hidden subtlety.
Sentence Translations (English): This music is extraordinarily fine.
His plan is marvelous.
A masterly hand restores spring.
This writing is peerlessly beautiful.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The fine, hidden character of something that is difficult to perceive directly.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): The word suggests profound subtle operation rather than ordinary cleverness.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The outward limits, traces, or visible effects through which something can be perceived.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): It contrasts visible external effects with the hidden subtlety of 妙.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Identifies the two immediately preceding realities as the subject under discussion.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): It points back deictically to the paired modes of 無 and 有.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): The number or pair consisting of two entities.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): It denotes a complementary pair rather than an undifferentiated plurality.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): A nominalizing particle that turns the preceding numeral phrase into a designation for persons or things.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): It makes 兩者 mean ‘the two things’.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Being one and the same rather than different in identity or kind.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): This adjectival use asserts identity rather than shared origin.
Sentence Translations (English): The two books have the same source.
This and that are identical.
Ruler and ministers are of one mind.
The two horses are the same color.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Indicates that two entities share an origin or condition.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it marks common origin, not identity of names or manifestations.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To move from inside or away from a place or group.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): This concrete motion sense differs from metaphysical origination.
Sentence Translations (English): The sun comes out in the east.
The guest goes outside the gate.
The army leaves from the outskirts.
The envoy exits the city.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To come forth from a source or originate out of something.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it describes common origination, not physical departure from a place.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Connects two sequential or related clauses or actions.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): Here it links common emergence with differing names.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To treat something as unusual or worthy of astonishment.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): This evaluative use expresses a reaction, not simple difference.
Sentence Translations (English): Everyone is surprised by his talent.
The ruler finds the minister’s words strange.
The villagers regard it as extraordinary.
I find this matter strange.
additional_senses.Translation (English): to regard as strange; to be surprised at

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Distinct from another in designation or character.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): The difference concerns names, while origin remains shared.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): To state something verbally or present it as a proposition.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): This use reports speech or an assertion rather than assigning a designation.
Sentence Translations (English): Confucius speaks of benevolence.
The historian says that he was good.
Everyone says it is impossible.
I say that the ruler understands.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): To designate or describe something by a particular term.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): 同謂之玄 means that both are called or characterized as profound mystery.

additional_senses.Dictionary Meaning (English): Having a very dark color or lacking light.
additional_senses.Nuance (English): This concrete color sense is distinct from the philosophical sense of profundity.
Sentence Translations (English): Dark clothing covers the body.
A black bird gathers in the forest.
Dark clouds obscure the sun.
A black banner is at the front.

contextual_sense.Dictionary Meaning (English): Beyond ordinary understanding because its operation is deep, hidden, and difficult to define.
contextual_sense.Nuance (English): It denotes profound obscurity and generative mystery, not merely intellectual difficulty.
